summary: When a workflow is cancelled while awaiting start_child_workflow(), the CancelledError is swallowed instead of propagating, causing the workflow to continue running instead of being cancelled. The issue is suspected to be related to shield() preventing proper cancellation handling.
userImpact: Users cannot reliably cancel workflows that are awaiting child workflow execution, as the cancellation request is silently ignored and the workflow continues running.
rootCause: The shield() call in start_child_workflow prevents CancelledError from propagating correctly; the exception handling around it needs to explicitly handle workflow cancellation.
proposedFix: Review and update the exception handling around the shield() call to ensure workflow cancellation (CancelledError) is not suppressed.
resolutionDetails: Exception handling around shield() in start_child_workflow was updated to properly propagate workflow cancellation.
keyQuote: It seems the start_child_workflow is shielding from CancelledError, which might explain why the cancelled exception is swallowed.
